period.ancient.shortDescription: Early civilizations, c. 3200–900 BC: from the beginnings of writing through the Bronze Age and into the early Iron Age, including early Mesopotamia and Egypt. The 900 BC boundary is a catalogue convention; these civilizations continued afterward.
period.antiquity.shortDescription: Classical antiquity, c. 900 BC–AD 500: ancient Greece and Rome, alongside contemporary Mediterranean and Near Eastern civilizations, through the fall of the Western Roman Empire.
period.early_middle_ages.shortDescriptio: The early medieval period, c. AD 500–1000, following the decline of the Western Roman Empire. Includes the Anglo-Saxon kingdoms, the Carolingian world, and much of the Viking Age.
period.high_middle_ages.shortDescription: The central medieval period, c. AD 1000–1250, marked in Europe by growing towns, castles, crusades, and expanding trade. Some regional chronologies extend it to around 1300.
period.late_middle_ages.shortDescription: The later medieval period, c. AD 1250–1500, including the Hundred Years’ War, changing armor and clothing, and the growth of urban life. The Renaissance began during this period in parts of Europe.
period.renaissance.shortDescription: For this catalogue, Early modern covers c. 1500–1700: the Reformation, overseas expansion, the Thirty Years’ War, and the English Civil War. Renaissance culture continued into this period, having begun earlier. The 1700 boundary is a browsing convention; academic chronologies often extend Early modern to around 1800.
period.modern.shortDescription: Modern / pre-WWI, c. 1700–1914: the eighteenth century through the outbreak of World War I, including the American and French revolutions, the Napoleonic era, and industrialization. The world wars and interwar years have separate categories.
period.wwi.shortDescription: World War I, 1914–1918: the global conflict that began on 28 July 1914 and ended in an armistice on 11 November 1918. Followed by the Interwar period.
period.interwar.shortDescription: Interwar, 1918–1939: the years between World War I and World War II, including postwar reconstruction, the 1920s, the Great Depression, and major political and technological changes. Related conflicts in Asia began before 1939.
period.wwii.shortDescription: World War II, 1939–1945: the global conflict conventionally dated from 1 September 1939 to 2 September 1945, with related conflicts in Asia beginning earlier. Followed by Contemporary times.
period.contemporary.shortDescription: For this catalogue, 1945–present: the postwar era, including the Cold War, decolonization, and more recent history. Begins at the end of World War II.
period.other.shortDescription: No fixed date range. Use for material that does not fit the listed categories; add specific years to the record when known.
